batch: C03c.2 continuous physical-event rates and balanced event approach

environment.timeout_scope: Harness timeout, not a measured performance acceptance bound.

source_hash_scope: Committed compiled source for the optimized worker run. Native development and final native runs have the separate source states recorded below. Hashes cover local working-tree bytes of the committed files.

root_causes.event_rate: Continuous incoming solutions had cancellation-sized static residuals which, divided by a tiny reverse-charge derivative, produced artificial rates of order 1e13 V/s. Retained companion history provides a physically audited rate predictor.
root_causes.event_clock: A 0.4 ps BestAvailable high-injection probe left a 1.3937993321518516e-22 s interval before the 2 ns event. The companion charge subtraction corrupted algebraic KCL. Balancing the two unaccepted approach intervals changed this landing interval to approximately 2e-13 s and the independent accuracy test passed.
root_causes.diagnostic_scope: These are local execution traces, not live ngspice/Xyce comparisons or performance qualification.

implementation.rate_reference: Only a continuous event with retained integration coefficients and identical individual authored/delayed forcing values may supply a companion-current predictor. Transmission-line history remains excluded from this predictor pending its own certificate. Startup keeps its separate authenticated OP contract.
implementation.reference_admission: A predictor must fit the original physical row backward-error budget. Floating-component storage rows share the remaining omitted-node KCL budget, reserving half for factorization roundoff. Invalid references fall back to the sampled physical RHS.
implementation.normalization_change: Finite storage-rate audits now retain physical F contribution scales, matching the existing original KCL audit instead of normalizing solely by the already-cancelled net F. Differentiated algebraic rows retain their per-second normalization. This is an explicit normalization correction; user tolerances and independent oracle limits were not increased.
implementation.invariants: No capacitance removal, current deletion, device-law change or source-clock relabeling. Original charge, rank, finite physical KCL/flux and prescribed slope audits remain.
implementation.scheduling: For an adaptive physical approach without another exact endpoint, split a tail shorter than half the proposed interval across two unaccepted intervals. Preserve the model floor, existing source/model/controller bound, and exact future event clock; retain the existing subminimum-gap fitting policy.
implementation.checkpoint_identity: v100 for rate initialization; v101 for balanced physical-event approach.

coverage.transient_unit_scope: 574 passed, zero failed, one pre-existing diagnostic ignored in the final selected transient run. Earlier focused runs overlap; do not sum them as distinct cases.
coverage.private_node_matrix: 42 public run_tran calls: three bias regimes, NPN/PNP, Ngspice/Xyce/BestAvailable; actual RB=25, RC=5, RE=2 ohms and 100/200/50 ohm external loads. Independent manufactured native Fourier forcing, terminal KCL, intrinsic voltages reconstructed through Ohm law, current accuracy and refinement.
coverage.refinement_protocol: Ngspice/Xyce retain 40 ps/4 ps requests. BestAvailable retains the original 4 ps current/voltage gates and adds a 0.4 ps run for the unchanged 0.7 error-reduction gate against 40 ps; assert at least twice as many accepted samples. Its nominal 40 ps request was already adaptively close to the 4 ps grid. No claim that the original BestAvailable 4 ps refinement ratio passed.
coverage.native_integration_scope: 75 tests across seven targets, zero failures/ignores. Includes checkpoint continuation, cancellation, source events, resource ceilings and atomicity.
coverage.wasm_scope: 22 tests across four targets, zero failures/ignores, on committed optimized source in a headless Chrome dedicated worker. Enabling veriloga-wasm-jit does not establish external model/JIT qualification.

resolved_development_failures: Unconditional integration references did not satisfy Xyce weighted static/history equations; references became predictors checked against physical budgets.
Independent retained-row budgets could violate the floating component omitted KCL row; the final implementation shares that remaining budget.

The new floating-component unit fixture initially supplied a small standalone current without the large cancelling terms described by its intent. Corrected to stamp those terms. All three integrated-rate unit tests passed the focused rerun, and all selected transient units passed the final broader run.

A scripted field rename also touched an existing integration module path and parameter, causing compilation errors in gp-driven-reference-transient-unit.log. Those unintended edits were reverted before the subsequent unit runs.
The finer BestAvailable matrix exposed the separate physical clock tail failure; scheduling was repaired without widening numerical gates.
remaining: All C00-C14 packages remain open; this closes the two named private-node regressions, not C03 or overall production readiness.
C03c still requires separate Weil feedback/private-node oracles, further parameter/cutoff/depletion/overlap/temperature/scaling cases and rejection/restart/OP/UIC coverage where applicable.
C03d physical-event providers remain missing, including the explicit behavioral-source reproducer and other excluded families/instances.
Whole-run allocation/memory limits, inner-solve cancellation latency, remaining configurations and measured performance limits remain open.
No new live ngspice/Xyce run, full-crate test run, or application/platform certification is claimed.
